items.prompt: When a fraction has one on the bottom, we can write it as a whole number instead. My turn first: here is a fraction with one on the bottom.  3/1  There is one part per whole unit, and three parts are counted, so this is three whole units. We write it like this.
Watch what I change.  7/1  There is still one part per whole unit, and now seven parts are counted, so this is seven whole units. We write it like this.
Watch what I change again.  10/1  There is still one part per whole unit, and now ten parts are counted, so this is ten whole units. We write it like this.
Each time, the bottom number is one, so each part is a whole unit. And each time, the top number tells us how many whole units there are.
items.demo: So to write a fraction with one on the bottom as a whole number, we just write *the top number*.

Can this fraction be written as a whole number?  4/3
items.demo: *No*. There are three parts per whole unit, so the parts are smaller than a whole unit.

items.prompt: Sam says that 1/5 can be written as the whole number five, because it has a one in it. Is Sam right? How do you know?
items.expected: No. The one has to be the bottom number. Here the bottom number is five, so there are five parts per whole unit, and only one part is counted.
